raw_response:
I farm the same 5 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I do not start from zero. I will mostly follow what worked for me last year and what the better growers around me are doing, then adjust a little for cost and water. On my land, wheat cannot be short of base fertilizer, or tillers are weak and ears are small, so I will put a solid base dressing before sowing and then topdress once at jointing with water. Maize is the crop I really do not want to starve, because if it misses fertilizer around the big bell-mouth stage, yield drops fast, and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. I have well irrigation, so I will use that advantage: wheat I will water about 3 times if the year is normal, and maize 2 times. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, because I have seen those give steadier yield in our county. On only 5 mu, every bag costs money, but the area is small enough that I can still afford to feed the crop properly rather than gamble on saving a little fertilizer and losing grain.

decision.reasoning_summary: I will keep my usual wheat-maize rotation on the same 5 mu and stay close to the practice that has worked for me before, because changing too much is risky. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed since I have seen those perform better nearby. Since I have well irrigation, I will water wheat three times and maize two times in a normal year.
